To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have established a cell line from a differentiated squamus carcinoma of the naspharynx, that this line has been successfully propagated in vitro, and that it has the ability to form tumors when injected into athymic nude mice.
a cell line has been established from a recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma that has a squamous epithelial morphology and a karyotype that is aneuploid.

a new squamous epithelioid cell culture line was established from the nasopharyngeal cancer of a Chinese patient, and the cell line was shown to be of human origin and to be of the same type of cancer as that from which the cells originated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of a cell line derived from a differentiated squamocellular carcinoma of the naso‐pharynx of a human Chinese male.

the establishment of a cell line from a differentiated squamocellular carcinoma of the naso‐pharynx, and the morphologic, karyotypic, virological, and transplantation characteristics of this cell line.

establishing a cell line derived from a recurrent well‐differentiated human squamous carcinoma of nasopharynx, and the characterization of the cell line with respect to the histological and ultrastructural features, growth properties, and the chromosomal constitution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this cell line does not have EBV infection.
the cell line was not established from an EBV‐associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
the cells are of human squamous carcinoma origin, but that the presence of the Epstein‐Barr virus cannot be excluded.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a well‐differentiated epithelioid squamous carcinoma cell line, NPC/HKI, from the nasopharyngeal region of a Chinese male, has been successfully established.
the cells from the cell culture line are of human origin and are derived from a differentiated squamocellular carcinoma of the naso‐pharynx.

we have been able to culture a cell line from a differentiated squamocarcinoma of the nasophanyx, which on transplantation into athymic nude mice, forms tumors morphologically identical to the original human tumor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have successfully established a human cell line from a differentiated squamocellular carcinoma of the naspharynx, which is similar to the original tumor from which it was derived.
a long‐term cell line has been established from a recurrent well‐differentiated nasopharyngeal squamous carcinoma.
a cell line was established that retains the morphologic features of the original tumor.
